title: Multiplying and dividing decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000

steps.say: Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1,000 moves every digit 1, 2 or 3 places to the left.

head: Ones
Tenths
Hundredths
Thousandths
figure.alt: A place value chart. 0.045 moves two places left to make 4.5.

steps.say: Dividing by 10, 100 or 1,000 moves every digit 1, 2 or 3 places to the right.
Use this to change units. Changing to a smaller unit needs more of them, so multiply.
Changing to a bigger unit needs fewer of them, so divide.
Learn the links between units. Each one tells you whether to use 10, 100 or 1,000.

head: Unit
Equals
figure.alt: A table of unit links: 1 cm is 10 mm, 1 m is 100 cm, 1 km is 1,000 m, 1 kg is 1,000 g and 1 l is 1,000 ml.

hints: Multiplying by 100 moves the digits two places.
The digits move to the left.
check.explanation: Each digit moves two places to the left, so 0.38 × 100 = 38.

hints: Dividing by 100 moves the digits two places.
The digits move to the right.
check.explanation: Each digit moves two places to the right, so 6.4 ÷ 100 = 0.064.

check.prompt: A bottle holds 0.75 litres of juice. How many millilitres is that?
hints: Multiply the number of litres by 1,000.
Move each digit three places to the left.
